chunks: And with this chain of narration - from Yunus from Mu'awiya from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
"That among the stored-up merits is the completion [of the pilgrimage] in the Two Sanctuaries."

key_terms.الْإِتْمَام: Completion or finishing (of the ritual rites)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The Two Sanctuaries, referring to Mecca (Al-Haram) and Medina (Al-Masjid Al-Nabawi)
key_terms.الْمَذْخُور: Stored-up merit or treasure; good deeds accumulated for the hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'al-madkhur' in the context of Hajj completion?
ai.summary: In the context of expiation for pilgrims' inadvertent errors, this hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights that the true spiritual merit lies not merely in performing rituals, but in their complete and proper execution within the Two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina). This underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *itmam* (completion/perfection) as a key component of valid worship, linking ritual precision to spiritual reward.
